cards.title: PING
cards.description_long: The 'ping' command checks if a host is reachable over the network and measures response time. It’s essential for basic network diagnostics.

main_commands.explanation: Send ICMP packets to google.com to check connectivity
Send only 4 ping packets and stop
Send ping packets with 1000 bytes payload
Set the TTL (time to live) value for ping packets

activity: Ping a website and observe response time
Send a limited number of ping packets

cards.title: IP
cards.description_long: The 'ip' command is used to display and manage network interfaces, IP addresses, routes, and more. It’s a modern replacement for many older networking commands.

main_commands.explanation: Display all network interfaces and their IP addresses
Show link layer information for interfaces
Add an IP address to an interface

activity: Check IP addresses assigned to interfaces
Assign a temporary IP to an interface
Bring an interface up or down

cards.title: IFCONFIG
cards.description_long: The 'ifconfig' command shows network interface configuration. It can also be used to enable/disable interfaces and assign IP addresses.

main_commands.explanation: Assign a new IP to eth0

activity: Display all interfaces on the system

cards.title: TRACEROUTE
cards.description_short: Trace the path to a host
cards.description_long: The 'traceroute' command shows the path packets take to reach a destination host. It’s useful to identify where network delays occur.

main_commands.explanation: Do not resolve IP addresses to hostnames
Use ICMP ECHO instead of UDP packets

activity: Adjust number of probes per hop
Use ICMP instead of default UDP packets

cards.title: SS
cards.description_long: The 'ss' command shows socket statistics, including TCP, UDP connections, and listening ports. It’s a modern alternative to netstat for monitoring connections.
